ai.description: The Kashmir Rock Agama reaches 30 cm. It is grey-brown with dark, irregular blotches and a yellow-spotted throat. Distinctive features include a flattened body and enlarged, keeled scales on the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Laudakia tuberculata* is best distinguished by the enlarged, sharply pointed, and strongly keeled scales on its flanks, which are significantly larger than those on its back.
ai.habitat: The Kashmir Rock Agama inhabits rocky outcrops and cliffs in the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 3,500 meters within temperate forest zones.
ai.behavior: The Kashmir Rock Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently basks on sun-exposed boulders to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laudakia tuberculata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between May and July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laudakia tuberculata* inhabits the Western Himalayas, ranging from Jammu and Kashmir to Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand at elevations between 1,000 and 4,000 meters.
